title: Implement the six repository functions over SQLite
notes:
§5.3, exactly six exports and nothing more: upsertSession, getSession, getSessionByKey, recordEvent, getEvents, listOpenSessions. This is the ONLY module in the tree allowed to write SQL or import the sqlite driver (§6.2).

Contract details the doc implies but does not spell out: getSession/getSessionByKey return undefined for no match (not null, not a throw); getEvents parses data from JSON text and yields null where the column is null; getEvents orders by id ascending; recordEvent against a missing session_id must fail rather than write an orphan - enable foreign keys.

upsertSession is deliberately one function for both create and transition (§5.3) - do not split it.

Done when: unit tests against an in-memory database cover all six, and getEvents returns rows oldest-first with data already parsed.

title: Build the Session registry and its emitter for CREATED and WAITING
notes:
§6.2 Session module and the §3 state machine, but only the two states this slice needs: CREATED on create, WAITING when the patient socket connects. No grace timer, no ACTIVE, no ENDED transitions beyond what the start-up sweep needs.

Hard rule: Session imports persistence never, holds no keys, reads no chat. It owns an in-memory registry keyed by sessionId and a typed emitter that fires on each transition and each presence change.

Done when: every unit test for this module runs with no socket, no HTTP and no database, and a transition emits exactly once.

title: Subscribe the event recorder to the Session emitter
notes:
§6.2 'Event recorder'. A subscriber, not a caller: it attaches to the Session emitter at start-up and turns each emission into a recordEvent call, and each transition also into an upsertSession call.

The point of this task is that the state machine never writes to the database. The one exception is createSession, which writes the first sessions row itself because only that path holds the keys.

Done when: driving a Session transition in a test with no HTTP layer present leaves the expected events row and updated sessions row behind.

title: Add Services: createSession, resolveKey, endInterruptedSessions
notes:
§6.2 Services, three of the five functions - getSessionEvents and getChatHistory are out of scope for this slice.

createSession: node:crypto randomUUID for the id and randomBytes for the two keys (§2.1), writes the first sessions row and the session_created event, adds to the registry, returns the two links. The response must not contain sessionId (§4.1, §4.2).
resolveKey: returns { sessionId, role, status } or nothing. The role derivation in §4.1 lives in this one function and nowhere else - the caller never declares its role.
endInterruptedSessions: the §3 start-up sweep. Every non-ENDED row moves to ENDED reason 'interrupted' with the event written. It must run before the server accepts a request, and must not touch the registry (empty at that moment).

Done when: restarting the server turns a previously ACTIVE row into ENDED/interrupted and a later request with that key gets session_ended.

title: Serve POST /api/sessions and GET /api/sessions/:key on one http.Server
notes:
§4.2, first two rows only - the events endpoint is out of scope. Express 5 attaches to the same http.Server Socket.IO will use: one listener, one port (§2.1).

Every path param and body parses through a shared schema; no handler reads a raw param (§4.2). Parse failure returns { code: 'invalid_message', message } at 400; no session for that key returns unknown_key at 404 (§4.5). Deliberately the same code for a missing key and for a patientKey on a provider-only route - a distinct code would leak that the session exists.

HTTP holds no state machine code and no SQL - it calls Services or Session only.

Done when: curl POST /api/sessions returns the four fields and no sessionId, and GET with a bad key returns 404 { code: 'unknown_key' }.

title: Wire the Socket.IO handshake middleware, room join, and first session:state
notes:
§4.3. This is the server half of 'client connects and says hello'. There is no hello event and this task must not add one - the handshake carries the key and the first session:state is the reply.

io.use middleware: read auth.key, call resolveKey, attach sessionId and role to the socket, join room session:<sessionId>. Refuse with unknown_key (no match), role_already_connected (that role already has a socket), or session_ended (state ENDED). Emit session:state to the socket on connect.

Config: pingInterval 10s, pingTimeout 20s. Do NOT enable connectionStateRecovery (§4.3 says why). Write no heartbeat code.

Hard rule: Signaling never imports persistence. It maps events to Services or Session calls and decides nothing about state.

Done when: a socket.io-client with a valid key connects and receives session:state; with a junk key it gets connect_error carrying { code: 'unknown_key' }.

title: Convert the client to React and wire the session/socket layer
notes:
packages/client/src/main.ts is currently one innerHTML line. Install react, react-dom, @vitejs/plugin-react and socket.io-client (none are installed). Make packages/client/tsconfig.json extend ../../tsconfig.base.json and set jsx: react-jsx - it extends nothing today.

Session/socket layer per §6.3: knows nothing about either view, wraps the §4.2 HTTP calls and the Socket.IO client, turns socket events into React state, uses the shared types. One socket for the whole app. It holds NO reconnect or backoff code - socket.io-client does that. A middleware refusal is not retried, so on connect_error show a terminal screen; do not add a retry on top.

Key goes in the handshake - io(URL, { auth: { key } }) - never in a URL (§4.3: URLs reach history, Referer and access logs).

Provider and patient views are separate top-level components, not one component with a role condition (§6.3). Minimal UI: role, state, error. No media layer, not even a stub.

Done when: two tabs on the provider and patient links each render the state they received over the socket.

title: Widen vitest include to .tsx and confirm the test convention
notes:
vitest.config.ts line 5 is include: ['packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts'] - it matches no .tsx, so client tests written per §6.4 would silently not run. Widen to *.test.{ts,tsx}.

§6.4: tests sit next to the code they test. Do not add a __tests__ directory. The top-level tests/ project for e2e is out of scope for this slice.

Done when: a deliberately failing .test.tsx under packages/client/src is picked up by npm test.

title: Create packages/shared with the Zod contract from section 4
notes:
New workspace @coviu/shared. Root package.json workspaces glob is already packages/*, so no change there. zod is NOT installed yet - add it here.

One schema per HTTP body/response (§4.2), one per Socket.IO payload (§4.3), plus the SessionStatus union (§3), ended_reason union, event type union (§5.2) and ErrorCode union (§4.5). Every exported type via z.infer - no hand-written interface may duplicate a schema. Also export ClientToServerEvents and ServerToClientEvents built from those inferred types.

Trap: writing these is where §4 gets tested against itself. If a payload in the doc is underspecified, fix docs/architecture.md in the same change - a doc/code disagreement is a defect in one of them (top of that file). Do not paper over it downstream.

Done when: both other packages can import @coviu/shared and a wrong Socket.IO event name fails tsc, before any runtime schema runs.

Built @coviu/shared as source-only (package.json main/types/exports all point at src/index.ts, no build step) so tsx and Vite's bundler resolution pick it up directly. Files: status.ts (SessionStatus/EndedReason/Role), errors.ts (ErrorCode/ErrorPayload), events.ts (EventType + per-type data schemas + Event), http.ts (the three §4.2 endpoints, including the events endpoint even though it's out of scope for the current plan slice - the shared contract covers the whole doc), socket.ts (all §4.3 payloads plus ClientToServerEvents/ServerToClientEvents). Verified the 'wrong event name fails tsc' requirement with a throwaway smoke file in packages/server before deleting it. Added @coviu/shared as a real dependency in server and client package.json (needed for the import to resolve under NodeNext/bundler resolution) - not just documentation, actual wiring. Deleted the packages/shared line from architecture.md §8 and narrowed the remaining dependency-gap bullet to the still-missing ones.

title: Add the SQLite schema for sessions and events
notes:
Tables exactly as §5.1 and §5.2: sessions (with the ended_reason CHECK constraint) and events (AUTOINCREMENT id, JSON text data column) plus idx_events_session_id. Created on start-up if absent, at data/app.db.

Decision from the plan: use node:sqlite, not better-sqlite3. This machine is Node 26.6 where node:sqlite is stable, and §2.1 says prefer it. Remove better-sqlite3 from packages/server/package.json and add engines: { node: '>=22.5' }.

Done when: a fresh checkout with no data/ directory starts and 'sqlite3 data/app.db .schema' prints both tables, the CHECK, and the index.

Implemented in packages/server/src/persistence/schema.ts (applySchema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for sessions/events + idx_events_session_id, per §5.1/§5.2) and database.ts (openDatabase: mkdir data dir if absent, opens node:sqlite DatabaseSync, runs applySchema). index.ts calls openDatabase('data/app.db') on startup. Removed better-sqlite3 from packages/server/package.json, added engines >=22.5, ran npm install to drop it from the lockfile. Added data/ to .gitignore. Tests: schema.test.ts and database.test.ts against in-memory / tmp-dir databases, covering column shape, the CHECK constraint (rejects bad reason, accepts the three valid ones, allows NULL), the index, idempotent re-apply, and directory creation on a fresh path. Verified manually: rm -rf data && npx tsx packages/server/src/index.ts && sqlite3 data/app.db .schema prints both tables, the CHECK, and the index - matches the done criterion exactly. Repository functions (upsertSession etc, cth-3) are NOT implemented here - out of scope for this task.
